argument:
The bull correctly separates an income purchase from an earnings-acceleration thesis. Stable H1 profit, 17.8% total capital and 0.98% gross impaired financing give an 8.20x earnings and 7.01% reported-yield proposition substantive support. Missing CET1 or financing margin should not erase those verified starting strengths.

The remaining issue is earnings conversion and distribution resilience: financing grew 7.5% while H1 profit rose just 0.5%, and total capital is not the same loss-absorption measure as CET1. The incomplete supplement and unknown posting date constrain precision without proving adverse change. A low multiple can compensate for modest growth, but not guarantee payouts if funding spreads or credit costs worsen. I accept cautious income ownership as defensible; the argument against aggressive adding is limited margin visibility and weak timing, not absence of all bank-risk evidence.
key_points: Verified capital and asset quality support an income proposition.
Financing growth has produced limited H1 earnings conversion.
Missing detailed margins constrain conviction rather than imply deterioration.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers that income need not require rapid growth and has real bank metrics. The unresolved margin and payout sensitivity warrants bounded conviction, not a blanket rejection of the low-multiple income case.
